newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian stocks close firm, seen lacking strength.
newsitem.headline: Austrian stocks close firm, seen lacking strength.

text.p: Austrian shares closed firmer on Friday, boosted by firm international leads and buoyant bond markets, but traders said the market was unlikely to have the strength to build on its gains over the next few days.
Traders said the underlying sentiment remained bearish, adding that Monday's dividend payout in Creditanstalt could put further pressure on the overall market.
"I expect the index between 1,180 and 1,200 points," said one, adding the full impact of lower-than-expected U.S. employment figures released earlier on Friday had yet to be felt.
"We'll have to wait what Wall Street thinks about the figures", he said.
Market participants traced most of the day's gains to advances in selected shares, particularly engineering group VA Technologie and steel maker Boehler-Uddeholm.
"The market was trailing behind VA Techologie and Boehler", one trader said, adding that overall volumes had been thin.
The ATX blue chip index rose 11.48 point or 0.96 percent and closed at 1,205,71. Among the ATX constituents, 14 shares closed higher, five were down and two unchanged.
VA Technologie led the day's gainers to close up 2.95 percent at 1,949 schillings after announcing a 2.2 billion schillings new order in Venezuela.
Boehler gained 20 schillings to close at 899.
Paper maker Leykam Muerztaler were up four schillings at 296 following news of a healthy first-quarter profit, compared to a loss a year ago.
OMV closed barely changed at 1,329,90, down 0.10 schillings on the day. The group said it would release its preliminary first-quarter figures on Monday.
The May ATX future closed at 1,1194, a gain of six points.
